cards.text: Last chapter of Numbers, friend. The family heads of the clan of Gilead, from Manasseh, one of the clans of Joseph, walk up to Moses, Israel's leader, and the heads of Israel's families. They want to talk about their relative Zelophehad and the land the LORD said would be his family's inheritance.

cards.question: The family heads remind Moses what the LORD already commanded. Zelophehad's inheritance is to go to his ___.

cards.text: Then they lay out the problem, and it's a big "what if." I bet these men ran this scenario more times than I've checked an oven timer.

cards.question: If Zelophehad's daughters marry men from other tribes of Israel, what do the family heads say happens to their land?

answers.text: It is added to the tribe they marry into
It goes back to Moses to give out again
It is split up among the tribe of Levi

cards.text: Then they bring up the Jubilee. Friend, these men aren't planning for next week, they're planning all the way out to the JUBILEE.

cards.question: The family heads say that when the Jubilee comes, the daughters' land will go back to the tribe of their fathers.

cards.text: Moses doesn't wing this one. He answers at the word of the LORD, and trust me, every time I wing a batch, the smoke alarm has something to say.

cards.question: Moses answers the family heads from the clan of Gilead, part of the tribe of the sons of Joseph. What does he say about their concern?
Moses gives the LORD's command about Zelophehad's daughters. Who are the daughters allowed to marry?

answers.text: Anyone they please within their father's tribe
Only men that Moses chooses for them
Only men from the priestly tribe of Levi

cards.text: Then the rule gets BIGGER: no inheritance in Israel may be transferred from tribe to tribe. And Moses gives the reason.

cards.question: Why can't an inheritance in Israel move from one tribe to another?

answers.text: Each Israelite keeps his fathers' tribal land
All the land belongs to the Levites
The lots can never be cast a second time

cards.question: The rule to marry within a clan of their father's tribe is only for Zelophehad's daughters and no other daughter in Israel who inherits land.

cards.text: Moses says it one more time: each tribe of Israel must keep its inheritance. Now it's up to Zelophehad's daughters.

cards.question: Moses has passed along the LORD's command about who they can marry. What do Zelophehad's daughters do next?

answers.text: They obey and do as they were told
They ask Moses to change the ruling
They give the land to their uncles

cards.text: Here are the sisters, by name: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah. And no, friend, not the Noah with the boat.

cards.question: The daughters of Zelophehad were married to ___ on their father's side.
After the daughters marry within the clans of Manasseh, their inheritance stays within the tribe of their father's clan.

cards.text: And that's how Numbers wraps up: these are the commandments and ordinances the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. The land stays with the family, friend, the same way this gold base stays with me.

findings.problem: The card's last line, 'The land stays with the family,' retells Numbers 36:12, where the inheritance remained within the tribe of their father's clan. The card cites only Numbers 36:13, so its citation is too narrow. It should be Numbers 36:12-13.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of a thought. It continues the earlier ruling about Zelophehad's daughters (Numbers 27:1-11), but the opening card never says that Zelophehad died without sons or that the LORD had already given his inheritance to his daughters. Without that context, card 2 ('his ___', answer daughters) is pure luck, and the daughters' marriage 'problem' on cards 3 and 4 has no setup. The opening card should briefly give this background with its reference, without stating the card 2 answer outright.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.
